row.name: Southwest Route
row.overview: A long, scenic PCT approach to a camp at Snowy Lakes, followed by an easy scree-and-talus scramble that ends in one short, exposed low-5th-class move to the true summit.
row.approach: Drive SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to Rainy Pass (4,880 ft) near milepost 158, about 35 miles west of Winthrop or 51 miles east of Marblemount. Park at the Rainy Pass North (PCT) trailhead. Hike north on the Pacific Crest Trail through forest and switchbacks to Cutthroat Pass (~6,800 ft), continue past Granite Pass (~6.25 miles in, where snowfields can linger into August) and along a cliff-cut trail toward Methow Pass. About a mile before Methow Pass, a small, unsigned spur trail switchbacks up to Lower and then Upper Snowy Lake (~6,700–7,000 ft) — roughly 10–11 miles and 2,700 ft of gain one-way from the trailhead. Good campsites sit in the meadow near the lakes.
row.descent_text: From the summit, most parties make a single short rappel (roughly 40 ft; a 30m rope is plenty) off the summit block to regain the ridge, then downclimb/scramble class 2–3 scree and talus back toward Snowy Lakes — plunge-stepping the loose scree speeds this considerably. From camp, retrace the PCT approach back over Granite and Cutthroat Passes to Rainy Pass.
row.best_season: Prime conditions run roughly July through October, once seasonal snow has cleared from Cutthroat and Granite Passes and the upper mountain. Late September into early October is the most popular window, when western larches along the PCT turn gold — but this also brings heavy trailhead and camp congestion at Snowy Lakes. May and June ascents are possible but typically require an ice axe (and sometimes crampons) for lingering snow on the passes and near the summit.
hazards: Loose rock and scree are the primary objective hazard on the approach gully and summit block.
The exposed traverse/mantle onto the true summit carries real consequences despite its short length.
Afternoon thunderstorms are common on the exposed upper ridge in summer.

row.name: East Face
row.overview: A longer, harder technical line up Tupshin's east face, reached via a demanding cross-country approach from Company Creek over a pass above Bird Lakes; class 2-4 ledge scrambling leads to a short, poorly-protected 5.4-5.6 crux below the summit.
row.approach: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin (no road access), then the Company Creek Trail roughly 3 miles to a point below Tupshin's west side. Leave the trail and scramble up White Goat Mountain's west slopes through dense brush, traversing rightward through the 4,200-4,600 ft band, then cross a roughly 7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes and descend into the Bird Lakes basin below Tupshin's east face (face starts ~7,600 ft). Most parties in July to September go in by the Devore Creek trail to the Bird Creek camp near 5,400-5,500 ft, then fight slide alder up to a basin camp around 5,800 ft; easy slopes lead to a ridge near 7,000 ft, then a descending traverse to the snow basin east of the summit block.
row.descent_text: Downclimb the summit pitch and upper class 4 terrain back through the ledge system, taking care around the crux flake/crack; parties have used a 30 m rope for the technical sections. Continue down the zigzagging ledges and the lower class 2-3 ramp back to the basin below the face, then reverse the cross-country traverse over the pass above Bird Lakes to Company Creek Trail.
row.best_season: July through September; snow/moat conditions at the base of the face (~7,600 ft) can persist into early summer, and the approach traverse holds snow into July in big years.
hazards: Long, complex, brush-and-talus approach with genuine route-finding difficulty
Sustained exposure through the ledge system with a sparsely-protected crux
Total remoteness — no cell coverage, no road access, rescue is slow
